Memo submitted. Summary of where things landed:

**Flux lines over both thresholds (>10% and >$5,000)**

| Acct | Line | Feb | Mar | Change | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5000 | Hosting & Infrastructure | 31,301.80 | 40,948.20 | +9,646.40 (+31%) | **Explained** |
| 6300 | Travel | 785.40 | 7,158.41 | +6,373.01 (+811%) | **Not verified** |
| 6400 | Marketing Programs | 7,898.14 | 29,686.00 | +21,787.86 (+276%) | **Not verified** |

**Hosting holds up at the ledger level.** The recurring Stackline production invoice actually fell $153.60 (JE-00125 → JE-00232). The whole increase is JE-00258, Stackline SC-M-2203, a $9,800 "one-time data migration" — the math ties exactly. Caveat: I did not get to open the invoice, so classification (expense vs. capitalizable) and the one-time nature should be confirmed before you accept ~$31k as the April run-rate.

**Travel and Marketing are open.** I burned the tool budget pulling balances for every expense account and only got as far as Hosting detail and February Travel detail before being cut off. Those two lines are $28.2k of the $33.7k total move, so the flux is not sign-off ready. That was a sequencing mistake on my part — I should have pulled detail on the big movers before sweeping every zero-activity account.

**Two things you should know beyond the threshold lines:**
- **March depreciation (6800) is $0** vs $3,425 in Jan and Feb; YTD is unchanged at $6,850. The March entry appears not to have been posted.
- **March bank fees (6900) are $0** vs $65 in prior months — immaterial, but likely unrecorded.

No entries were posted and nothing was matched or reversed. The memo lists five follow-up items for the controller in Section 4.
